clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old man with Crohn's disease (managed with sulfasalazine) presented to the emergency department with sudden onset paraplegia, abdominal pain, and bilateral lower extremity pain with numbness. Physical examination revealed impalpable femoral and distal pulses, pale and cold legs with flaccid paralysis, sensory loss from the umbilical level (T10) distally, and fecal incontinence with loss of sphincter tone. Laboratory findings showed metabolic acidosis (pH 7.2, base excess −13 mmol/L, lactate 6.2 mmol/L) and elevated creatinine (155 µmol/L), indicating tissue ischemia and acute kidney injury. CT angiography of the whole aorta revealed extensive aortic thrombosis extending from the diaphragm to the aortic bifurcation without atherosclerosis. Open exploration confirmed extensive visceral ischemia. Endovascular interventions including thrombectomy and stenting of the right renal artery, superior mesenteric artery, and distal aorta were performed immediately post-CT. Massive reperfusion edema required bilateral leg fasciotomies. Second-look surgery at 24 hours revealed viable abdominal organs except the gallbladder, which was removed. The patient required 2 days of ICU-level care with mechanical ventilation. After 3.5 months of inpatient spinal rehabilitation, the patient regained some sensory function of the lower extremities but remained wheelchair-dependent, indicating permanent neurological sequelae from spinal cord ischemia.
